title: EV Charger Rebates in Los Angeles 2026: Up to $1,500 from LADWP | HomePowerRebate
desc: LADWP pays up to $1,000 for a Level 2 home charger, $500 more for income-qualified customers and $250 for a dedicated EV meter. Rules, rate discount and steps.
h1: EV Charger Rebates in Los Angeles
badge: Up to $1,500, plus $250 for a meter
lead: LADWP pays up to $1,000 for a Level 2 home charger and $500 more for income-qualified customers, with another $250 if you add a dedicated EV meter. It also offers a discount of 2.5 cents per kilowatt-hour for charging on that meter.
cards_intro: These figures come from LADWP's Residential EV Charger Rebate Program page, which we read on October 2, 2026. The account holder named on the bill, with an active meter on a residential rate, can apply.

cards.title: Level 2 charger
cards.note: For a qualifying charger: 240 volt, tested by a recognized lab, network-capable, with a SAE J1772 or J3400 connector.

cards.title: Income-qualified customers
cards.note: For customers in the Senior Citizen/Disability Lifeline or EZ-SAVE programs, for up to $1,500 in total.

cards.title: Dedicated EV meter
cards.note: Choose the meter option on the charger application.

cards.title: EV rate discount
cards.note: Applies to base period charges on a separately metered EV charger on a time-of-use rate, with a $10 monthly minimum.

after_cards:
What the whole job can earn

A qualifying charger earns up to $1,000, and a dedicated EV meter adds $250, so a standard customer can reach $1,250. An income-qualified customer in the Lifeline or EZ-SAVE programs can reach $1,750. The rate discount then lowers your charging cost every month, but only if the charger is on its own meter and that meter is on a time-of-use rate.
sections:
LADWP says to book a service assessment before you install the charger, to help prevent problems. Use its Find the Right Person page, enter your address, and contact the representative listed in the Residential Electric Vehicle section. The assessment tells you whether your service and panel can carry the charger. Ask for it before you buy, because a charger you cannot power is a wasted purchase.

LADWP also asks you to complete a Residential EV Charger Request form if you need electrical service for the charger.
The meter, the rate and the math

The dedicated meter earns $250 and unlocks the 2.5 cent discount, but it adds a $10 monthly minimum charge. For a household that charges a lot overnight, the discount can outweigh that. For someone who drives little, it may not. Ask the LADWP program specialist at (866) 484-0433 or PluginLA@ladwp.com for a worked example for your usage.
LADWP lists a separate used EV rebate of up to $4,000 on its EV page. We did not read those terms, so check them on the LADWP site before you rely on the figure.

LADWP's charger rebate is larger than Pasadena's $600 (Pasadena) and Burbank's $500 (Burbank), and it is the only one of the three with a published EV rate discount. Glendale's rebate list has no EV charger rebate. LADWP says its charger rebate will continue even though the federal credit for home chargers ends for projects placed in service after June 30, 2026.
claim_heading: How to claim the LADWP charger rebate
claim_steps: Check that you are the account holder on an LADWP residential rate with an active electric meter.
Book a service assessment with LADWP before you install.
Choose a qualifying Level 2 charger from LADWP's qualifying product list.
Have it installed, and a dedicated EV meter if you want the extra $250 and the rate discount.
Apply online through your LADWP account, or mail the application to LADWP Residential EV Charger Rebate Program, PO Box 51111, Room 1019, Los Angeles, CA 90051-0100.
If you are on Senior Citizen/Disability Lifeline or EZ-SAVE, say so on the application for the extra $500.
faq: How much is the LADWP EV charger rebate?
Up to $1,000 for a qualifying Level 2 charger, plus $500 for income-qualified customers and $250 for a dedicated EV meter.
LADWP account holders whose name is on the bill, with an active LADWP electric meter on a residential rate plan.
Level 2 (240 volt), certified by a nationally recognized testing laboratory, network-capable, with a SAE J1772 or J3400 connector.
What is the EV rate discount?
$0.025 per kWh on base period charges, for an EV charger on a separate meter that is on a time-of-use rate.
Does the rebate end when the federal credit ends?
LADWP says its EV charger rebate will continue after the federal credit expires.
